title: Six Killed as Helicopter Crashes Near Joshimath on Badrinath to Dehradun Flight
excerpt: A Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter carrying five Bengaluru passengers and its pilot crashed into a hillside near Joshimath on Friday; the operator's fleet has been grounded.
body:
• All six people on board a Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter died when it crashed into a hillside near Joshimath, Uttarakhand, on Friday afternoon.
  • The helicopter took off from Badrinath at about 1:14 p.m. bound for Dehradun and crashed near the JP Power House at Marwari Bridge around 2:20 p.m.
  • The dead are pilot Captain Himanshu Sabharwal of Delhi and five passengers from Bengaluru, including police inspector Arun Salunke.
  • The Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority has grounded Trans Bharat Aviation's entire fleet while the cause is investigated.

Six people were killed on Friday when a private helicopter flying from Badrinath to Dehradun crashed into a hillside near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, police said. The aircraft, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt. Ltd., was carrying five passengers and its pilot when it went down near Chai village, close to the JP Power House and Marwari Bridge.

Chamoli Superintendent of Police Surjit Singh Panwar confirmed that all six occupants died and that their bodies had been found at the wreckage site. Teams from the district administration, police, the State Disaster Response Force, the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police were sent to the hillside to recover the remains and secure the site, according to PTI reporting in The Hindu BusinessLine.

The flight and the victims

The helicopter, registration VT-HCX, took off from the Badrinath civil helipad at about 1:12-1:14 p.m. on Friday, headed for the Sahastradhara heliport in Dehradun. According to the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), the aircraft lost communication while crossing the Joshimath valley and its tracking stopped registering, Mirror Now reported. The crash was reported at around 2:20 p.m.

The pilot was identified as Captain Himanshu Sabharwal, 48, a resident of Shalimar Bagh in Delhi. The five passengers were all from Bengaluru: Arun Salunke, 44, a police inspector attached to the Bengaluru Police Crime Branch; H.S. Nataraj, 51; Sudhir K., 49; Shankar Gowda, 39, a lawyer; and Prathapa. The passengers had arrived in Uttarakhand on Wednesday. The Karnataka government said the mortal remains of all six had been recovered and were being taken to Joshimath for post-mortem examination, with the Karnataka Chief Minister's Office coordinating with Uttarakhand authorities to bring the remains home.

Weather, grounding and the investigation

The crash happened on a day when the India Meteorological Department had issued an orange alert for Chamoli district, warning of thunderstorms with lightning, hail and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph in isolated areas. Officials have not established whether weather, a technical fault or another factor caused the crash, and a formal investigation is expected to follow.

As a precaution, UCADA ordered the grounding of Trans Bharat Aviation's entire fleet. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said he was monitoring the situation and had directed the district administration, the Disaster Management Department and the SDRF to conduct a joint operation.

What happens next

Investigators will examine the wreckage, the operator's maintenance and flight records, and the weather at the time of the flight. Helicopter services ferry thousands of pilgrims and visitors through Uttarakhand's high valleys each season, and the findings will be watched closely by operators and regulators responsible for mountain flying in the state.
